args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 failed health checks in production (healthy=false, error rate 18%) in us-east, us-west and eu-west. The release candidate v2.3.1-rc had also been unhealthy in staging. Rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy and the error rate is 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause in v2.3.1 before redeploying, and check why it was promoted even though the staging RC was unhealthy.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened the SEV2 incident.

- **Rollback:** The latest deploy, v2.3.1, was failing health checks with an 18% error rate in us-east, us-west and eu-west. v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to that. All three regions now run v2.3.0, and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api) is open and has paged on-call. It describes the failure, the rollback and the recovery.

v2.3.1 shouldn't be redeployed until the root cause is found. Its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) also failed health checks in staging, so it's worth finding out why it was promoted to production anyway. I put both of these in the incident as next steps.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
